papers_read.title_as_printed: Memory-driven eye movements prospectively predict dementia in people at risk of Alzheimer’s disease

Drawing a line?—Visuo-constructive function as discriminator between healthy individuals, subjective cognitive decline, mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer’s disease and predictor of disease progress compared to a multimodal approach

what_each_reports.P-988: Parra, Granada and Fernandez 2022 (Alzheimers Dement DADM 14:e12386), matching the record. 65 MCI patients and 42 controls at AXIS Neurociencias, Bahia Blanca, followed for 40 months. A model based on baseline eye movements during the ~10-minute VSTMB task was applied blind to clinical decisions. The article text does not specify the model; it cites the authors' earlier work (refs 12, 25) and the Supplementary Material. It predicted that 36 of the 65 MCI patients would progress to the AD clinical syndrome (ADS). 34 of the 36 (94%) met ADS criteria by year 3, and none of the 29 predicted non-progressors developed ADS (5 frontotemporal dementia, 2 Parkinson disease, 4 vascular dementia, 7 major depression, 11 still MCI). In-sample ROC on groups defined at follow-up: MCI stable vs MCI-to-ADS AUC 0.95 (sens 95%, spec 95%); MCI-to-ADS vs MCI-to-other-pathology AUC 1.0. No external cohort and no confidence intervals.
what_each_reports.P-991: Tokaj and Lehrner 2024 (Neuropsychiatr 38:71-81), matching the record. Retrospective analysis of a Vienna memory-clinic cohort (33 HC, 68 SCD, 301 MCI, 220 AD); 117 returned at 12-48 months (mean 24.02). Converters to the next stage (n=23) and stable returners (n=94) did not differ in baseline MMSE (p=0.1), CDT (p=0.210) or VVT 3.0 (p=0.116). Within the original MCI group (n=76; 14 progressed to AD): MMSE AUC 0.808 (cut-off 27.5, sens 78.6%, spec 71.0%, PPV 0.38, NPV 0.94), CDT 0.497, VVT 3.0 0.488. The authors conclude that none of the three tests can be recommended to reliably predict progression, and that 'solely the MMSE showed some validity'. Its MMSE AUC of 0.972 is for AD vs non-AD diagnosis, not the contested quantity.

quantity_a: Prognostic accuracy of a baseline VSTMB eye-tracking model (fixation duration, saccade amplitude) for conversion from MCI to the clinically defined AD syndrome within about 40 months, in 65 MCI patients at one Argentine clinic; reported as predicted-vs-observed counts and as in-sample ROC AUC on groups defined at follow-up.
quantity_b: Prognostic value of baseline MMSE, Sunderland CDT and VVT 3.0 Screening scores: for progression to the next diagnostic stage (HC, SCD, MCI, AD) over 12-48 months among 117 returners (Mann-Whitney on baseline scores), and for MCI-to-AD in 76 MCI patients (ROC AUC); Vienna memory clinic, retrospective analysis.
incompatible_if_same: Not on the record's own question. The record asks whether a brief clinic test can carry prognostic signal, and in each paper one brief test did: P-988's eye-tracking model with AUC 0.95 within MCI, and P-991's MMSE with AUC 0.808 within MCI. The directions agree. Only by treating different instruments as one quantity could P-988's 0.95-1.0 be set against P-991's CDT and VVT (0.497 and 0.488). Neither paper reports a confidence interval for these prognostic AUCs, so even the eye-tracking vs MMSE contrast could not be shown incompatible from the reported uncertainty.

gates.task: mismatch on the registry (T2 vs T1); match in substance on the contested sub-analysis, since P-991's progression analysis is also progression prediction in MCI
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: AXIS Neurociencias, Bahia Blanca (Argentina) vs the Vienna Conversion to Dementia Study (Medical University of Vienna); no waiver on record
gates.validation_tier: match: both V2 (internal only, no external cohort)
gates.modality_family: mismatch: oculomotor recording (fixation duration, saccade amplitude) during a memory-binding task vs paper-and-pencil test scores (MMSE, CDT, VVT 3.0); no waiver on record. The record's 'behavioural assessment' family lumps the two together

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: P-988's endpoint is conversion from MCI to the clinically defined AD syndrome within 40 months, measured as predicted-vs-observed counts and as in-sample ROC on groups defined at follow-up. P-991's endpoint is conversion to the next stage (HC to SCD, SCD to MCI, MCI to AD) over 12-48 months among returners (tests on baseline scores), plus MCI-to-AD within 76 MCI patients (ROC AUC).
performance_validity: The flag applies to P-988 on the PDF, although the pack marks it false. The ROC AUCs are 1.0 (MCI-to-ADS vs MCI-to-other) and 0.95 (MCI stable vs MCI-to-ADS), on groups defined at follow-up in the same 65-patient single-site cohort, with no external cohort. The headline split (34 of 36 predicted converters converted; 0 of 29 predicted non-converters progressed to ADS) implies sensitivity 34/34 and accuracy 63/65 = 0.969 (reader's computation from the reported counts). The article text does not specify the prediction model (it cites earlier work and the Supplementary Material), so its independence from this cohort cannot be checked. This candidate is a prognostic-performance comparison, so it could not be genuine on this ground alone. P-991 does not meet the flag: its AUC of 0.972 is for AD-vs-rest diagnosis in n=622, not the contested quantity.
independence: Distinct studies, cohorts and author groups; no shared participants. Each paper's authors have a commercial interest in the instrument they evaluate: two P-988 authors are ViewMind officers, and P-991's Lehrner heads the company whose website distributes the VVT 3.0. This bears on each study's own reliability, not on non-independence between them.
grounds: The record's own resolution presents both findings as true ('Both findings stand') and attributes the difference to static test scores versus task-embedded eye movements. That is an 'architectural fork', which the rule records as a false positive (record resolution; P-988 p3 and P-991 p6 quotes show the different instruments).

The two papers evaluate different instruments: P-988 its VSTMB eye-tracking model, P-991 the MMSE, Sunderland CDT and VVT 3.0. Neither tests or makes any claim about the other's instrument, so a positive result for one and a null for the others is a claim about X set against a claim about Y (P-988 p3 quotes; P-991 p6 quotes).

The record misreads P-991 as a blanket null on brief-test prognosis. Within MCI, the MMSE reached AUC 0.808, and the authors conclude that the MMSE 'showed some validity'. On the record's own question, whether a brief clinic test can carry prognostic signal, both papers therefore answer in the same direction (P-991 p6 and p10 quotes; P-988 p7 quote).

The record says P-991's progression arm is 'genuinely prospective prediction' and 'the same quantity P-988 targets'. P-991 contradicts this: it is a retrospective analysis, and its progression endpoint is conversion to the next stage over 12-48 months among 117 returners (P-991 p3 and p6 quotes).

Read as a disagreement, the pair would fail as documented incommensurability. Predictor set, endpoint and horizon, sample and metric all differ, and the dataset-family and modality-family gates fail with no waiver on record (quotes above).

It could not be genuine in any case. As a prognostic-performance comparison, it rests on P-988's near-ceiling in-sample discrimination (AUC 1.0; 63 of 65 classified correctly) in 65 patients at one site with no external cohort (P-988 p1 and p7 quotes).

record_defects: claim_b and description call P-991 'a direct negative result on brief-screen prognostic sufficiency' in which none of the three tests predicts progression. P-991 reports MMSE AUC 0.808 (sens 78.6%, spec 71.0%) for MCI-to-AD within 76 MCI patients, and concludes that the MMSE alone 'showed some validity'. Its null is specific to its own three tests, and complete only for the CDT and VVT 3.0.

Description: 'three standard brief tests fail progression prediction in a 622-patient cohort'. The progression analyses use the 117 returners (23 converters vs 94 stable) and the 76-patient MCI subgroup, not 622.

Description: 'P-991's progression arm is genuinely prospective prediction (117 follow-ups), the same quantity P-988 targets'. P-991 is a retrospective analysis, its progression endpoint is conversion to the next stage (HC to SCD, SCD to MCI, MCI to AD) over 12-48 months, and it tests different instruments from P-988.

Description: 'Both studies ask whether a brief (<15 min) clinic assessment can carry prognostic signal across the AD continuum'. P-988's prognostic analysis is confined to MCI, and its full assessment session lasted 1.5 h (the VSTMB component about 10 min). Prognosis was only P-991's second aim.

Description: 'The signal P-991 cannot find in scores is exactly what P-988 extracts from behaviour-during-task'. Neither paper tests this: P-988 reports no prognostic analysis of its own MMSE or ACE-R scores, and P-991 records no eye movements.
demotion_note_2026_08_29: 'all four deterministic gates fail'. The validation tier matches (both V2, internal only); task (registry T2 vs T1), dataset family and modality family differ.

[registry row, not the ledger record] P-988's Best_Metric says 0% of non-ADS-progressing patients 'developed dementia', but Section 3.4 lists 5 frontotemporal and 4 vascular dementias among them, so the 0% holds only for ADS (P-988's abstract has the same inconsistency). Its primary_metric_type 'Acc' is not a figure the paper reports.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A same-instrument result would change it: for example, P-991 evaluating VSTMB eye tracking, or P-988 evaluating MMSE, CDT or VVT prognostically, with the opposite finding under a comparable endpoint and horizon. Neither paper does. If the adjudicator reads the record as asserting a disagreement rather than a fork with both findings true, the fallback outcome is documented_incommensurability: predictor set, endpoint and horizon, sample, and the dataset and modality families differ, with no waiver. Genuine is excluded under either reading by the performance-validity flag on P-988.
